svg.text: ZIRH-3 - the compute die, as built (the SoC-import ladder is complete)
every block lints clean and holds its replicas through synthesis: 70 measured TMR replicas / 4192 flops, checked in CI on every push (scripts/check_tmr.sh)
the die's own reset and observer clock:
hold, re-arm on dropout + the independent
sys_rst_n - the conditioned reset every block runs on (also the gate, clkobs, bank, hk, tlm)
ro_clk + ro_rst_n - the independent observer domain
clock-loss observer on the die's own
oscillator: sees a main-clock SEFI the
synchronous die cannot, latches the sticky
one pad, two listeners: the ISP receiver and the CPU console RX
image, READ-BACK verify of STORED words,
holds the CPU, programs the bank through
bus with timeout + the shared UART.
The ISP mux holds, programs, releases;
the TX mux interleaves CPU bytes and
slot 2 UART - slot 3 hk - slot 4 bank
boots ROM or the loaded bank
a committed bank SIGNS ON when its firmware writes CPU_SIG (hk pulses cpu_alive);
the watchdog verdict is grace-gated one full period; a watchdog revert counts as a
reject - isp_hold never re-arms against the golden CPU
v2 frames into the shared TX
the SEU counters (plain vs TMR A/B,
raw and escaped), ECC and bus-timeout
tallies, boot count, the CPU SIGNATURE
CPU bytes on the one TX pin

zirh3_top - takes only clk + pad reset + power-good and makes everything else itself; boots ROM or a loaded image, runs code in its ECC bank, reports on telemetry, reverts a bad bank, offers ISP and JTAG behind their protection boundaries
Provenance: every block arrived at its proven state from zirh2 with its suites, formal proofs and synthesis-integrity numbers attached; the measured
replica/flop checks run in CI on every push. The pad ring, ESD and physical macro hardening remain the named new-design area (docs/SCOPE.md).
The gate this repository is built around: B10 - integration is complete, tape-out waits for ZIRH-1/2 beam data. ZIRH-2 measures; ZIRH-3 is what the measurements are for.
